label: Early original-phase token-pair detector (t=1-2: input in {c,v,i,2,d,q,3} after {2,3,c,l,h,x,1,d})
explanation: Fires almost only in the original phase at steps t=1 (71% of mass) and t=2 (29%); essentially never at t=0, t>=3, the delimiter, or the copy phase. Within those steps it acts like a lookup on the (previous token, current token) pair: the current input must be one of c, v, i, 2, d (and more weakly q, 3, l, o, x), and the activation is strongest when the previous token is a digit 2 or 3 or one of c, l, h, x, 1, d. The largest activations are 2 or c followed by c or v at t=1-2 (e.g. 3 2 c, 3 2 v, c 2 c). Activation is larger at t=1 than at t=2 and when the token is appearing for the first time. The predicate gets F1 about 0.70 and mass recall about 0.87 on dev. What it misses is a long tail of weaker pairs outside these sets (e.g. c o, 3 x, c q), and some predicted pairs stay below threshold, so the token sets only approximate a graded pairwise response.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: c, v, i, d, 2, q; least: b, z, t, e) and the previous input (most: 2, 3, c, l, h, x; least: e, b, n, j); timing cues that raise it most: t=1, t=2, L=3 & t=5.
